I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the steadiest way for me to earn and manage risk. I am 70, so I do not want crops that need too much hand labor or too much market guessing. Winter wheat and summer maize fit my experience, the machines are easy to hire, the input-output is familiar, and I know how to manage water and fertilizer for them. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, because I care more about stable yield than saving seed myself.

For management, I will keep things simple and practical. I will plough before wheat so the soil holds water better and the straw mixes in well. For maize after wheat, I will use no-tillage direct seeding to save time and labor. I will not push fertilizer too hard, because that raises cost and can lodge the crop, but I will still feed enough nitrogen for yield, with phosphorus and potassium for root growth and grain filling. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat in this area depends more on timely watering. I will spray only as needed, mainly for common diseases, worms, and weeds, and I will keep the number of applications limited because I want control without wasting money. My goal is steady production and lower labor pressure, not chasing the absolute highest yield.
